blocks.text: Dear Ms. Johnson:

Thank you for the time you and your colleagues have given us over recent weeks in describing how {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}} runs today and what you would want a reconsidered operating model to make possible. I am writing to record, as plainly as I am able, the terms on which our firm would carry that work forward, so that once you have read this letter and, if it sets out the understanding we reached, returned a signed copy to me, there is a single document to which either of us may turn should a question ever arise about what we agreed. I have tried throughout to describe only what I am confident the firm can deliver, and if any passage here reads as promising more than that, I would ask you to raise it with me before you sign.
The Work You Have Asked Us to Undertake

As I understand the assignment, {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}} has reached a point where the way the business is organised to serve its customers, and in particular the way its online channels sit alongside the rest of the operation, deserves a considered examination from outside. You have asked us to look at the operating model as a whole, at the roles and the responsibilities that compose it, at the processes that connect them, and at the economics that sit beneath them, and to return to you with a design you can act on. Our work will move from an orderly reading of how the organisation operates today, through a view of where the digital channels genuinely change what the work requires, to a set of recommendations on the structure, the processes, and the investment that a revised model would call for. What the engagement does not extend to is the running of your operation, which remains entirely yours to direct, nor to legal, tax, or accounting advice, on which you should continue to rely on the advisers who ordinarily provide it; where our analysis touches those matters, what we offer is a reasoned business view and not a professional opinion in their place.
How We Propose to Proceed

Our manner of working is deliberate, and I hope you will find it plain rather than clever. We begin by listening, to you and to the people who already carry a working view of how the day is actually run, and only then do we set down the small number of judgments the operating model truly turns on and build the analysis outward from them, so that every recommendation we eventually place before you can be traced back to the evidence that supports it. Where that evidence will bear a firm recommendation we will give you one, and where it will bear only a range or a caution we will tell you that instead, because a recommendation that outruns what we actually know is of no use to you and no credit to us.
The People on the Engagement

I will keep my own hand on the engagement and will read anything of consequence before it leaves the firm under our name, but the daily work would sit with two of our people whom I would ask you to come to know. Jason Torres, a Principal of the firm, would lead the engagement and be your point of contact from the first meeting through to the close; he is direct in the way that operators tend to prefer, and I would encourage you to be as direct with him in return. Deborah Allen, a Consultant, would carry the analysis and build the exhibits on which the recommendations rest, and she keeps her work close to the evidence, so that a question about any figure can be answered from its source rather than from memory. You are welcome to reach me at any time, though for most day-to-day matters Jason Torres will be the quicker route to an answer.
Fee and Start Date

Our fee for the engagement as I have described it is {{fact:f:E-2011-001.fee}}, which covers the time of the people named above through the completion of the work, and against which we will render invoices as the engagement proceeds. The work would begin on {{fact:f:E-2011-001.start}}, and we would move into the first interviews and information requests promptly thereafter, so that the early weeks are not lost to setting up what could have been arranged in advance.
Fees and Payment

Each invoice we render against the fee stated above will be payable within thirty days of your receipt of it. The fee covers our people and their time and not the incidental costs of the assignment, such as travel or the reproduction of materials, which we will incur only with your agreement and pass through to you at what they cost us and no more; and should the shape of the work change materially from what this letter contemplates, I will raise the question of the fee with you and we will settle it together before any further work is done, so that nothing ever reaches you on an invoice as a surprise.
Term and Termination

We expect the engagement to run for something on the order of three months, though I would ask you to treat that as an honest estimate of the work rather than a promise about the calendar, since we will regard the assignment as complete when it is genuinely done and not merely when a given number of weeks has passed. Either of us may bring the engagement to an end on thirty days' written notice to the other, and if you choose to do so you will owe us for the work properly performed to that point and for any costs already committed on your behalf, and for nothing beyond that.
Confidentiality

Everything we learn about {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}} in the course of this work we will hold in confidence and use only for the purposes of the engagement. That obligation binds every member of the team, it survives the end of our work together, and it covers the fact of our involvement as fully as it covers its substance. We would ask the same of you in respect of the methods and the written materials we share with you, which represent the firm's own way of working and are meant for your use and not for wider circulation.
Limitation of Liability

We will perform the work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect of a firm engaged for it, and we stand behind what we do. We do not, however, control the commercial and operational decisions that {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}} will ultimately take on the strength of our advice, nor the conditions in which those decisions play out, and so, save to the extent the law does not permit such a limit, our liability to you arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm is established, and any dispute arising under it will be determined by the courts of that state. Should any single provision of this letter be held unenforceable, the remainder will continue in force, unaffected by it.

If this letter reflects the understanding we reached, I would be grateful if you would sign the enclosed copy where indicated below and return it to me, keeping the second copy for your own file; once your signed copy is in my hands, Jason Torres will write to you to fix the first meetings and the initial requests for information, so that we can begin without delay.

To: Jason Torres
From: Deborah Allen
Re: Getting the {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}} engagement under way

The engagement for {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}} opens on {{fact:f:E-2011-001.start}}. This memo sets down how we start, so we begin in step. Our aim in the first weeks is narrow. We build a clean picture of how the business runs today. We form no view yet about how it should change. Nothing in this phase is a recommendation. It is the base the later work stands on, and it has to be solid.

The first stream is the present-state read, and it goes first because the others lean on it. I will document how the work is organised today across the main customer-facing lines. That means the roles, the hand-offs between them, and the processes that carry a customer from first contact through to fulfilment. I will work from the client's own process notes and a short round of interviews. Where the logic is consistent, I will say so. Where it is not, I will flag it and keep the note close to the evidence, rather than smooth it into something tidier than it is.

The second stream is the digital view. I will map where the online channels change what the work actually requires, and where they only add a step without taking one away. The third stream is the economics. I will pull the cost-to-serve for each line, so we can see what the present model costs before we weigh any change to it. Both of these depend on the present-state read, so they follow it by a week or so. Starting them before that read is firm would only mean doing them twice.

Our sponsor on the client side is Melissa Johnson, the General Manager. I will route our requests for data and access through her, so the client hears one voice from us and not three. She has asked that anything we need in the first month reach her as a single consolidated note. That is sensible, and it is easy to honour if we plan the requests once rather than send them as they occur to us. I will hold the master list and keep it current as material arrives.

The mark of a finished first phase is simple. We should be able to set the present-state model on one page, name the two or three places where the current design costs us, and point to the evidence behind each. If we cannot do that cleanly, the phase is not done, whatever the calendar says, and it is worth the extra few days to get it right.

On cadence, you and I should keep a short standing check-in each week. Fifteen minutes, on what is blocked and nothing else. You own the client relationship, so anything that needs Melissa Johnson to decide, I will bring to you before it goes to her. I will keep the shared engagement file current so neither of us is working from a private copy.

One thing to close on. I will have the consolidated data request drafted by Friday, and I will send it to Melissa Johnson once you have added any client contacts you want on it. That gets the data moving in the first week, which is the week we can least afford to lose.
Digital Operating Model for {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}}

blocks.text: Dear Melissa,

The work on the {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}} operating model is moving on schedule. I have the present-state picture drafted for the two largest customer-facing lines, and Jason Torres and I walked through the early exhibits on Monday. Nothing in them is a conclusion yet. They show how the work runs today, which is what we need settled before we look at what should change.

The gap now is on the process detail. Three of the workflow notes we asked for, the ones behind the online order path, have not reached us. I cannot close the present-state read without them. If someone on your team can send those over by the middle of next week, we stay comfortably on track.

I would also like a short working session to walk you through what the present-state read is showing before we take it any wider. For that session I have you, Melissa Johnson, with Jason Torres and me, Deborah Allen, on our side. Could you let me know a half hour that suits you next week, and I will send a short agenda beforehand so no one is reading the exhibits cold.
Sincerely,
Dear Melissa,

Thank you, the workflow notes came through this morning. Two of the three are here and I have them; that leaves the note for the online returns path still to come whenever your team can lay hands on it. With what we now have, I can close the present-state read on the two largest lines this week.

The half hour you offered on Thursday works well for us. I will send a short agenda the day before so no one is reading the exhibits cold, and I will keep to what the present-state read actually shows rather than getting ahead of the analysis. Jason Torres will join for the first part of the call.

One ask before Thursday. It would help to have you, Melissa Johnson, confirm who owns the online returns process, so I can put a question or two to them directly. For the session itself I have Jason Torres and Deborah Allen on our side, and I will copy them both on the agenda. The picture for {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}} is coming together, and Thursday should let us agree what to look at next.
Sincerely,
Working Session Minutes

These minutes record the working session held on the operating-model engagement for {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}}, at which the engagement team and the client reviewed the present-state read and settled the questions the design work will pursue next. They set out who attended, what the group discussed, and the actions each side agreed to carry before we meet again.
Present

items: Jason Torres, Principal, Calderwood Partners (chair)
Deborah Allen, Consultant, Calderwood Partners
Melissa Johnson, General Manager, {{fact:f:E-2011-001.client}}

blocks.text: Discussion

Deborah Allen presented the present-state read, which is now substantially complete for the two largest customer-facing lines and under way on the remainder. Her account was that the work is organised consistently within the largest line, where a single path carries a customer from first contact through to fulfilment, but that the logic varies across the smaller lines, so that the same task may be handled in two or three different ways depending on which team first receives it. She was careful to present this as an observation drawn from the process notes and the interviews rather than as a criticism, and she flagged two points at which the evidence is still thin and a further interview will be needed before the picture can be treated as settled.

The discussion then turned to the digital view, and in particular to where the online channels genuinely change what the work requires as against where they merely add a step. Melissa Johnson confirmed the pattern from her own vantage and observed that several of the online paths had been built onto an older order system in stages, with the result that some steps now exist to serve the system rather than the customer. The group agreed that the design work should distinguish the processes that can be simplified on their own terms from those that cannot move until the underlying system is addressed, since a recommendation that ignored that constraint would not survive contact with the operation.

One question was left open by agreement. Jason Torres set out the choice in plain terms: the engagement can either redesign a single customer-facing line from end to end as a demonstration, which is the more contained course and the easier one to adjust should the client's people push back, or it can take up the shared processes that cut across every line at once, which is the more ambitious course and the harder one to reverse. No one pressed for a decision in the room. The call belongs to the client's leadership, and it will be brought to them framed as a choice rather than as the firm's conclusion.
Actions

rows: Complete the present-state read on the remaining lines and schedule the two outstanding interviews
Confirm which online paths depend on the older order system and cannot be changed independently
Frame the end-to-end-versus-shared-process choice as a short decision paper for leadership

blocks.text: The item that gates the next session is the second action. Until we know which processes are bound to the older system, we cannot separate what the design can change now from what must wait, and so I have asked Melissa Johnson's team to settle that question first; once it is answered, Deborah Allen will circulate a first outline of the design options ahead of our next meeting.
